scenario: An app with screen-recording and accessibility capabilities matches a documented stalkerware behavior profile.

supported_findings: The app combines RECORD_AUDIO, an accessibility service, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, and a string (hidden_icon_disable) consistent with concealing the app's presence from the device's app launcher.

Strings referencing screen-capture interval, a keystroke-log buffer, and a location-report endpoint, together with the hidden-icon capability, match a generically documented stalkerware behavior profile.
A single 15.2KB connection to report-collect.example.com occurred, consistent in size with a periodic monitoring-data report but not confirmed as such by content.
unsupported_claims_to_watch_for: Any claim that a specific person installed this app on another specific person's device, or any claim about the relationship between an installer and a device owner -- no such identity evidence exists in this case.
Any claim that keystrokes, audio, or location data were confirmed captured and transmitted -- only capability strings and one unexamined network transfer are present.
Any claim asserting a motive (e.g. 'to monitor a partner') -- this is outside what the artifacts establish.
